podcast.body: The band's inaugural proper album, released in 1995, recorded for approximately $5,000. Distinctively, the album contained no electric guitars; all guitar sounds were achieved by running acoustic guitars through Marshall amplifiers. The first 5,000 copies of the album only bore the acronym "MGB" before the band officially adopted "The Matthew Good Band" due to popular demand. "The whole thing was recorded for about $5,000 and there were no electric guitars anywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Matt Good: In His Own Words - Part 1
